verdict.rationale: A hands-on probe got HTTP 200 for a real robots.txt at the trade-mark search host. Its directives restrict keyless agents, so an agent learns what it may not fetch before requesting anything else on that host. That meets the story's core even though the policy is restrictive. Missing for 10: the actual robots.txt directives are not quoted, there is no evidence of a robots.txt on the gov.uk guidance host or other IPO service hosts, and there is no first-party documentation of the crawl policy.
